title: When the Sigil Falls
premise: Cyrus Fairweather has spent her life carving bones into instruments of memory, keeping the Gilded Ledger guild's accounts of impossible trades while pretending she cannot hear the dead who whisper through her work. When prayers to the old gods begin landing answers instead of silence, Cyrus learns the thirteenth moon will crown a new king—except the crown is a god wearing the boy-king Aldric like a glove. To unbind him, she must trade with the dead for the one memory that can break the god's hold: her own inheritance of the bone-carving gift, paid forward by every Fairweather woman before her. In the end Cyrus gives up her ability to hear the dead forever, freeing Aldric and scattering the old gods back into prayer, and takes up a quiet life where silence, at last, is a choice.
about_author: L. M. Thackeray is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing funeral customs across three continents before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about grief, ledgers, and the stubborn arithmetic of love.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Cyrus audits the guild's strangest accounts—a bottled lullaby, a borrowed shadow—while the dead murmur through her carving tools. Her mentor Vess warns her to stay invisible as rumors spread of answered prayers in the eastern parishes. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: wary contentment built on denial.

chapters.title: A Prayer Answered
chapters.summary: A fisherwoman pays the guild in drowned memories to ask the old god Merrow for her son's return—and gets it, wrong-sized and dripping. Cyrus recognizes the returned boy's voice from her carvings. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: first crack in her safe distance; dread arrives wearing gratitude.

chapters.title: What the Bones Remember
chapters.summary: Cyrus carves a commission and accidentally hears the dead king's voice inside an heirloom femur, naming the thing on the throne: a god called the Thirteenth. Vess burns the bone and forbids further listening. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: forbidden knowledge as burden, not prize.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Is Not Alone
chapters.summary: Summoned to court to appraise royal relics, Cyrus meets King Aldric, sixteen and hollow-eyed, whose shadow moves a half-second late. The crown whispers to her through the gold. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: recognition between two people both being worn by something else.

chapters.title: Guild Politics, Grave Prices
chapters.summary: The Gilded Ledger's masters debate selling protection against the returning gods at ruinous rates. Cyrus realizes the guild profited from the gods' long sleep—and helped put them there. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: disillusionment; her employers become suspects.

chapters.title: Vess's Confession
chapters.summary: Dying Vess admits the Fairweather women were the original binders who sealed the old gods into relics, paying with their hearing, generation by generation. Cyrus is the last link in the chain. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: inheritance reframed as debt; grief braided with anger.

chapters.title: Thirteen Moons to Coronation
chapters.summary: An astronomer confirms the coronation falls on the thirteenth turn, when the Thirteenth god will fully wear Aldric. The countdown structure of the novel locks in. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: cold clarity; a deadline turns fear into purpose.

chapters.title: The Market of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Cyrus descends into the guild's black auction seeking a binding relic and witnesses a god's fingerbone sell for a city's worth of forgetting. She steals it rather than bid. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: transgression; crossing from observer to thief.

chapters.title: Hunted by the Faithful
chapters.summary: The Crown's new inquisitor, Dame Serah, hunts those who traffic with gods. Cyrus flees with the stolen relic, sheltered by the fisherwoman's impossible son, who remembers drowning. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: fugitive paranoia softened by unexpected kindness.

chapters.title: The Drowned Choir
chapters.summary: In flooded catacombs, the dead who loved the old gods sing their side of the story: they were bound not for wickedness but for hunger. Cyrus begins doubting the binding itself. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: moral vertigo; enemies gain faces.

chapters.title: Aldric's Letter
chapters.summary: Smuggled correspondence reveals Aldric is lucid in fragments, leaving coded pleas inside state documents. He knows what wears him and asks to be unmade if rescue fails. POV: alternating Cyrus and Aldric letters. Emotional beat: intimacy at a distance; resolve hardens into promise.

chapters.title: The Price Named Aloud
chapters.summary: The stolen fingerbone shows Cyrus the true cost of unbinding: a Fairweather must surrender the gift entirely, severing every dead voice forever—including Vess's, once she dies. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh; survival priced in silence.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Ledger House
chapters.summary: Cyrus returns to bargain with the guild masters and finds them negotiating with Dame Serah to hand over the last Fairweather. Vess's successor sells her out. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: betrayal; the institution she served chooses profit over blood.

chapters.title: Ash and Escape
chapters.summary: The Ledger House burns—by whose hand remains unclear—as Cyrus escapes with the guild's master ledger, which contains the original binding rites. Serah sees her face. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: scorched-earth flight; no way back to the old life.

chapters.title: Serah's Bargain
chapters.summary: Cornered, Cyrus discovers Serah lost her own brother to an answered prayer and wants the gods gone too—but by fire, not unbinding, which would kill Aldric. Uneasy alliance forms. POV: alternating Cyrus and Serah. Emotional beat: enemy empathy; two griefs, incompatible methods.

chapters.title: Reading the Rites
chapters.summary: Deciphering the ledger, Cyrus learns the binding requires a willing vessel and a moonlit threshold—the coronation itself could be turned into an unbinding. The plan crystallizes. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: hope with teeth; strategy replacing desperation.

chapters.title: The God Speaks
chapters.summary: The Thirteenth contacts Cyrus directly through carved bone, offering her anything—Vess healed, the dead returned—if she lets the coronation proceed. It shows her its centuries of loneliness. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: temptation rendered sympathetic; the hardest no.

chapters.title: Preparations and Farewells
chapters.summary: Allies gather: the drowned boy, Serah's defected soldiers, the fisherwoman's choir of grieving families. Vess dies, and Cyrus hears her final words before the end must come. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: tender assembly; love inventory before sacrifice.

chapters.title: Coronation Eve
chapters.summary: Infiltrating the palace via the bone-carver's traditional route, Cyrus reaches Aldric's chamber and meets the boy behind the god for the first time, whole and terrified. They agree on the signal. POV: alternating Cyrus and Aldric. Emotional beat: quiet before storm; courage chosen together.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: At the crowning, Cyrus begins the rite aloud before the assembled court. The Thirteenth fights through Aldric's body; Serah holds the guards; the dead choir sings the counter-prayer. Cyrus speaks the surrender clause. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: climax—chaos, faith, and a voice held steady.

chapters.title: What Silence Costs
chapters.summary: The god releases Aldric and, honoring the rite, offers Cyrus a choice: keep her hearing or free the god into peaceful dissolution. She chooses dissolution, and the dead go quiet mid-sentence—including Vess's unfinished goodbye. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: bittersweet triumph; victory measured in loss.

chapters.title: The Carver Who Hears Nothing
chapters.summary: Months later, Cyrus carves ordinary combs in a seaside shop, Aldric ruling gently under Serah's watch. A customer leaves a bone on her counter; she feels nothing, and smiles anyway. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: resolution—silence transformed from wound to peace, inheritance ended on her terms.
